description: The figure presents three pie charts under the heading “Zero-Shot,” comparing the distribution of four outcome categories across difficulty levels labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” with a legend on the right mapping colors to labels (teal = N+K+, yellow = N−K+, orange = N−K−, red = N+K−); each pie contains percentage labels inside the slices and none of the slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized. Each chart has 4 slices: for “easy,” N+K+ (teal) is about 55.4%, N−K+ (yellow) about 38.3%, N−K− (orange) about 4.6%, and N+K− (red) about 1.7%; for “medium,” N+K+ (teal) about 58.8%, N−K+ (yellow) about 35.4%, N−K− (orange) about 4.0%, and N+K− (red) about 1.8%; for “hard,” N−K− (orange) about 37.9%, N−K+ (yellow) about 37.3%, N+K+ (teal) about 18.1%, and N+K− (red) about 6.7%. Visually, the “easy” and “medium” pies appear arranged with the largest teal slice followed by yellow, then orange, then red, while the “hard” pie shows the two largest slices as orange and yellow, followed by teal and then red.
